title: The Example That Did Not Fit
title_ja: 当てはまらなかった例
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在の政策、医療指針、教育効果、調査結果ではない。台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Teachers often introduce a new concept through examples that display its most recognizable characteristics, because students need an initial opportunity to understand what the concept is intended to describe.
sentences.ja: 教師は概念が何を記述するか理解する最初の機会が必要なので、新概念を最も認識しやすい特徴を示す例で導入することが多い。

sentences.en: A carefully chosen example can make an abstract idea easier to discuss without requiring the learner to understand every possible application immediately.
sentences.ja: 慎重に選んだ例は、すべての応用を直ちに理解することを要求せず抽象的考えを議論しやすくできる。

sentences.en: However, students may occasionally learn to associate the concept with a feature of the original example that is not essential to the concept itself.
sentences.ja: しかし生徒は時に、概念そのものに不可欠でない元の例の特徴を概念と関連づけて学ぶことがある。

sentences.en: The distinction matters because a student can correctly recognize a familiar example while remaining uncertain about the underlying principle.
sentences.ja: 生徒は身近な例を正しく認識しても根底の原理には不確かさを残す可能性があるため、この区別は重要である。

sentences.en: Consider an imagined classroom in which students learn about the relationship between evidence and conclusions.
sentences.ja: 証拠と結論の関係を学ぶ仮想教室を考えよう。

sentences.en: The first example presents a scientific investigation in which several observations are recorded numerically and summarized in a table.
sentences.ja: 最初の例は複数の観察が数値で記録され表に要約される科学調査を提示する。

sentences.en: After examining several similar examples, a student begins to describe evidence as information that can be expressed in numerical form.
sentences.ja: 似た例を複数調べた後、ある生徒は証拠を数値形式で表せる情報と記述し始める。

sentences.en: The definition is consistent with a feature of the examples the student has encountered, but it is more restrictive than the concept the teacher intended to introduce.
sentences.ja: 定義は生徒が出会った例の特徴と一致するが、教師が導入しようとした概念より制限的である。

sentences.en: A historical document, for instance, may provide relevant evidence for a particular conclusion even when its contribution cannot usefully be summarized by a single number.
sentences.ja: 例えば歴史文書は、その貢献を単一数値に有用に要約できなくても特定結論への関連証拠を提供することがある。

sentences.en: The teacher therefore presents two contrasting cases that share the relevant relationship between information and a conclusion while differing in the form of the information itself.
sentences.ja: そこで教師は情報と結論の関連関係を共有しながら情報形式が異なる二つの対照例を提示する。

sentences.en: In one case, a conclusion is supported by a collection of measured values, whereas in the other it is supported by details found in written records.
sentences.ja: 一方では測定値の集合が結論を支持し、他方では文書記録に見つかる細部が支持する。

sentences.en: Students discuss what both cases have in common and which characteristics belong only to one particular example.
sentences.ja: 両例の共通点と片方だけに属する特徴を話し合う。

sentences.en: The activity is intended to encourage learners to revise their understanding of a general relationship rather than merely memorize a wider collection of familiar examples.
sentences.ja: 活動は単にさらに多くの身近な例を記憶するのでなく一般関係の理解を修正するよう促す。

sentences.en: An additional activity asks students to examine a claim accompanied by information that happens to be numerical but is unrelated to the claim being made.
sentences.ja: 追加活動では、数値ではあるが主張とは無関係な情報を伴う主張を調べる。

sentences.en: The presence of numbers does not automatically establish that the information provides an appropriate basis for the conclusion.
sentences.ja: 数値があるだけで情報が結論への適切な根拠を提供すると自動的に確定しない。

sentences.en: This example helps distinguish an outward feature of information from the function that information performs within an argument.
sentences.ja: この例は情報の外面的特徴と議論内で果たす機能を区別する助けになる。

sentences.en: The fictional lesson does not establish the effectiveness of a particular teaching method, which would require evidence from actual classrooms.
sentences.ja: 架空授業は特定教授法の有効性を確立せず、それには実際の教室の証拠が必要だ。

sentences.en: An example contributes to understanding when learners can recognize which of its characteristics are relevant to the concept under discussion.
sentences.ja: 例は学習者がどの特徴が議論中の概念に関連するか認識できると理解に貢献する。

sentences.en: Sometimes an example that initially appears not to fit provides a valuable opportunity to examine the assumptions behind a learner's original definition.
sentences.ja: 当初当てはまらないように見える例は、学習者の元定義の前提を調べる価値ある機会を提供することがある。

sentences.en: The aim is not necessarily to eliminate every uncertainty but to develop a more precise understanding of why different cases can be considered together.
sentences.ja: 目的は必ずしも全不確実性をなくすことでなく、なぜ異なる事例をまとめて考えられるかより正確に理解することだ。

sentences.en: Learning a concept therefore involves discovering where its boundaries lie as well as recognizing its most familiar illustrations.
sentences.ja: したがって概念学習には最も身近な例の認識だけでなく境界がどこにあるか発見することも伴う。

vocabulary.definition: relating to ideas rather than concrete objects
series of reasons supporting a claim

questions.prompt: Why can a familiar example be insufficient for learning a concept?
options: Students may mistake an incidental feature for an essential one.
It always contains information unrelated to the concept.
It makes every later application impossible.
It necessarily prevents students from recognizing the example.
questions.explanation_ja: 付随特徴を必須と誤解する。

questions.prompt: How does the student initially define evidence?
options: Any conclusion that a teacher states.
All information from historical documents.
Information expressible in numerical form.
A written explanation without data.

questions.prompt: What does the historical document example challenge?
options: The idea that evidence can support conclusions.
The assumption that evidence must be numerical.
The possibility of reading written records.
The value of scientific investigations.
questions.explanation_ja: 数値でなければ証拠でないという前提。

questions.prompt: What do the contrasting cases have in common?
options: Exactly the same form of information.
Identical numerical results.
A common historical date.
A relationship between information and a supported conclusion.
To memorize two separate definitions without comparing them.
To show that numerical evidence is never useful.
To identify shared essential features and incidental differences.
To eliminate any need for further examples.
questions.explanation_ja: 本質的関係を見つける。

questions.prompt: What does the additional activity present?
options: Numerical information unrelated to a claim.
A claim supported by every number shown.
An actual study proving a teaching method.
A test without any information.

questions.prompt: What is the significance of this additional case?
options: It shows every number qualifies as evidence.
It proves written records are always superior.
It prevents students from discussing an argument.
It shows a visible characteristic does not determine informational function.
Physical walls of the classroom.
Limits of what the concept includes.
The dates of several activities.
The amount of information recorded.

questions.prompt: Why can a seemingly unsuitable example be valuable?
options: It may expose assumptions underlying a learner's definition.
It guarantees an immediate correct definition.
It necessarily has no connection to the topic.
It removes every uncertainty about learning.
Learning concepts requires memorizing as many examples as possible without comparison.
A single familiar example always establishes complete understanding.
Numerical information should never be used as evidence.
Conceptual understanding develops by distinguishing essential relationships from incidental features of examples.
questions.explanation_ja: 本質的関係と付随特徴。

grammar.focus: without requiring the learner to understand
even when its contribution cannot usefully be summarized

paraphrases.source: A carefully chosen example can make an abstract idea easier to discuss without requiring the learner to understand every possible application immediately.
paraphrases.rewrite: A good initial illustration can clarify a concept without explaining every application.

paraphrases.source: A historical document, for instance, may provide relevant evidence for a particular conclusion even when its contribution cannot usefully be summarized by a single number.
paraphrases.rewrite: A historical record may support a claim without reducing its contribution to a number.

paraphrases.source: The teacher therefore presents two contrasting cases that share the relevant relationship between information and a conclusion while differing in the form of the information itself.
paraphrases.rewrite: Both cases share the essential relation but present information in different forms.

paraphrases.source: Learning a concept therefore involves discovering where its boundaries lie as well as recognizing its most familiar illustrations.
paraphrases.rewrite: Understanding a concept also means learning which cases fall within its scope.
